solutions.text: The passage states that splicing produces mature mRNA which is then translated by ribosomes, so the only role given to ribosomes is translation. Transcription (DNA to RNA) is performed by RNA polymerase, not ribosomes, so the claim that ribosomes transcribe DNA into RNA is contradicted by the passage. Every other statement is directly supported: exons are called coding regions, introns are removed before translation, splicing forms mature mRNA, and a gene is said to usually encode a protein.

The passage says beneficial mutations can increase in frequency over generations through natural selection, which only makes sense if selection acts on variation that already exists in the population. The other claims all contradict or overstate the text: it explicitly allows neutral and beneficial mutations (so not all are harmful), says only that beneficial mutations can increase in frequency (not that they always become fixed), gives no reason for neutral mutations to be quickly eliminated, and links fitness advantage to the mutation's effect rather than to the mutation rate itself.

The 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of nerve growth factor (NGF) went to Rita Levi-Montalcini, shared with the American biochemist Stanley Cohen. The other Italians won in different fields and years: Golgi for his staining method revealing nerve cell structure (1906), Luria for phage genetics (1969), Dulbecco for tumour viruses (1975), and Rubbia for physics (1984), none connected to NGF.

Ali finished before Bashir but after Chen, which fixes the partial order Chen, then Ali, then Bashir. Dev is stated to be last, so only fourth place remains for him and the full order is Chen, Ali, Bashir, Dev. No other arrangement satisfies both statements, so Chen finished first.

Catalysis is not exclusive to proteins: ribozymes are RNA molecules that catalyse reactions, and the peptidyl transferase activity of the ribosome itself is RNA-based. So the blanket claim is mostly true but has known exceptions, exactly as stated in the answer. Calling it always true ignores ribozymes, while calling it always false ignores that the overwhelming majority of enzymes are proteins.

TREE becomes USFF and each letter is shifted forward by one position in the alphabet: T to U, R to S, and each E to F. Applying the same rule to BIRD gives B to C, I to J, R to S, D to E, spelling CJSE. No other candidate keeps every letter shifted by exactly one.

The gaps between consecutive terms are 3, 5, 7 and 9, the successive odd numbers, so the next gap is 11. The next term is 27 + 11 = 38. Check: adding 3, 5, 7, 9 in turn to 3 gives 6, 11, 18, 27, confirming the pattern holds throughout.

Weekdays repeat with period 7, so only the remainder of 100 divided by 7 matters. Since 100 = 14 × 7 + 2, the remainder is 2, meaning 100 days from today falls on the same weekday as 2 days from today. Tuesday plus 2 days is Thursday.

The full dial is 360° divided into 12 hour marks, so each hour is 360 ÷ 12 = 30°. At 7:00 the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 7, i.e. 7 × 30 = 210° measured clockwise from 12. The angle between the hands is the smaller of 210° and 360 − 210 = 150°, so it is 150°.

The two strands of a DNA double helix run in opposite 5' to 3' directions: one strand runs 5' to 3' while its partner runs 3' to 5'. This geometric property is called antiparallelism. Complementarity instead refers to the A-T and G-C base pairing, supercoiling describes how the helix is coiled upon itself, and semiconservative describes the mode of replication.

In semiconservative replication each parental strand stays intact and acts as a template, so every daughter double helix contains one original strand and one newly synthesised strand. The Meselson and Stahl experiment confirmed exactly this. The conservative model, which would keep both parental strands together in one molecule and build a wholly new molecule in the other, is what the experiment ruled out.

Okazaki fragments are short pieces synthesised discontinuously on the lagging strand. DNA polymerase extends them but cannot close the final gap, so DNA ligase is the enzyme that seals the nick by forming the phosphodiester bond between adjacent fragments. Helicase unwinds the helix, primase lays RNA primers and topoisomerase relieves supercoiling, none of which joins fragments.

Transcription is the synthesis of RNA from a DNA template, catalysed by RNA polymerase. DNA polymerase copies DNA during replication, reverse transcriptase makes DNA from an RNA template in retroviruses, and helicase and ligase modify DNA structure rather than synthesising RNA.

The primary transcript (pre-mRNA) still contains introns, which are removed by the spliceosome during post-transcriptional processing called splicing; the exons are then joined into the mature mRNA. Translation reads only the finished message and never removes introns, and replication and DNA repair act on DNA, not on RNA.

The genetic code is read on mRNA in triplets, and each three-nucleotide sequence specifying one amino acid (or a stop signal) is a codon. The anticodon is the complementary triplet located on tRNA, while a promoter is the DNA region where transcription starts and an operon is a cluster of genes transcribed together.

tRNA carries the anticodon in its anticodon loop; this three-base sequence pairs with the complementary codon on mRNA so that the correct amino acid is delivered to the growing chain. mRNA carries the codons themselves and rRNA forms the structural and catalytic core of the ribosome.

The carboxyl group of one amino acid reacts with the amino group of the next, releasing water and forming a peptide bond (an amide linkage) between them. Phosphodiester bonds instead link nucleotides in nucleic acids, glycosidic bonds link sugars, and hydrogen bonds only stabilise the folded three-dimensional shape.

Secondary structure consists of regular arrangements of the polypeptide backbone, and both the alpha-helix and the beta-pleated sheet are stabilised by hydrogen bonds between backbone C=O and N-H groups. Disulfide bridges and hydrophobic interactions mainly stabilise the tertiary structure, and peptide bonds belong to the primary sequence.

2n = 6 means the diploid cell carries two sets of 3 chromosome types, six in total. Meiosis separates homologous pairs, halving the number, so each gamete receives one set, n = 3 chromosomes. Keeping 6 would describe mitosis, and 12 would be a doubling rather than a halving.

Step 1: the cross Tt × Tt produces genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt in a 1:2:1 ratio. Step 2: since T is dominant, TT and both Tt combinations are tall, so 3 of the 4 outcomes are tall and 1 is short, giving a phenotypic ratio of 3 tall : 1 short. The 1:2:1 figure is the genotypic ratio and does not describe phenotypes, while 9:3:3:1 belongs to a dihybrid cross.

A son receives the Y chromosome from his father, so his single X always comes from his mother. The carrier mother is XᴴXʰ, so each son has a 50% chance of receiving the Xʰ chromosome and being affected. The 25% figure would answer a different question, namely the chance per pregnancy of an affected child of unspecified sex.

The colour-blind father has only one X chromosome, and he passes that chromosome (bearing the recessive allele) to every daughter. The mother, who is neither colour-blind nor a carrier, always passes a normal X. Every daughter is therefore heterozygous XᶜXᴺ: a carrier whose normal second X masks the recessive allele, so none of them is colour-blind.

Step 1: for one gene, Aa × Aa gives a 3/4 dominant to 1/4 recessive phenotypic split. Step 2: with independent assortment the two genes multiply: (3/4)(3/4) = 9/16 show both dominant traits, (3/4)(1/4) = 3/16 for each of the two single-recessive classes, and (1/4)(1/4) = 1/16 show both recessive traits. This yields the classic 9:3:3:1 ratio.

Receiving a plasmid from another bacterium is conjugation, the classic case of horizontal gene transfer: DNA moves sideways between two living cells rather than being inherited from a parent cell. Mutation is a change within a cell's own genome, while mitosis, meiosis and transcription are cell division or gene expression processes that do not transfer DNA between cells.

Mitosis proceeds prophase (chromosomes condense, spindle forms), metaphase (chromosomes align on the equatorial plate), anaphase (sister chromatids separate and move to the poles), telophase (nuclear envelopes reform). Any ordering that puts anaphase before metaphase, or telophase first, contradicts these events, so the sequence is prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.

Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles filled with acid hydrolases that break down worn-out organelles and material taken into the cell, which is intracellular digestion. Ribosomes build proteins, mitochondria and chloroplasts produce ATP or sugars, and the nucleolus assembles ribosomal subunits.

Mitochondria, the site of aerobic respiration, occur in both plant and animal cells. The cell wall, the large central vacuole, chloroplasts and plasmodesmata are features of plant cells and are absent from animal cells, so only the mitochondrion is shared.

Glycolysis invests 2 ATP in its preparatory phase and regenerates 4 ATP in its payoff phase, for a net gain of 2 ATP, together with 2 NADH and 2 pyruvate molecules per glucose. The claim of 4 ATP quotes the gross production and forgets the 2 consumed, and FADH₂ is produced by the Krebs cycle, not by glycolysis.

Many enzymes need a non-protein helper to be active: an inorganic ion such as Zn²⁺ or Mg²⁺ is called a cofactor, while an organic helper molecule is a coenzyme. The apoenzyme is the inactive protein part without its helper, and the substrate is the molecule the enzyme acts on, so neither of those fits the description.

Motor neurons release acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction; it binds receptors on the muscle fibre membrane and triggers depolarisation and contraction. Dopamine, GABA, serotonin and glutamate are neurotransmitters of the central nervous system, not the junction with skeletal muscle.

In a resting neuron the inside of the membrane sits about 70 mV below the outside, maintained by potassium leak channels and the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, so the resting potential is approximately −70 mV. The value +30 mV instead corresponds to the peak of an action potential, not to the resting state.

Vitamin K is required for the gamma-carboxylation of clotting proteins such as prothrombin (its very name comes from Koagulation), so without it blood fails to clot properly. Vitamin C is involved in collagen synthesis, vitamin D in calcium absorption, vitamin A in vision, and vitamin B12 in red blood cell formation.
Amount of substance follows n = m ÷ M. Substituting the given values: n = 36 g ÷ 18 g/mol = 2 mol. The figure 18 is the molar mass itself, and 0.5 mol would correspond to only 9 g of water.

Step 1: balance carbon, 3 C in propane gives 3 CO₂. Step 2: balance hydrogen, 8 H gives 4 H₂O. Step 3: balance oxygen, the products contain 3 × 2 + 4 × 1 = 10 O atoms, so the reactant side needs 10 ÷ 2 = 5 O₂. The balanced equation C₃H₈ + 5 O₂ → 3 CO₂ + 4 H₂O checks on every element, so the oxygen coefficient is 5.
Each oxygen is assigned −2, so three oxygens contribute 3 × (−2) = −6. If x is the oxidation number of nitrogen, the sum over the ion must equal its charge: x + (−6) = −1, giving x = +5.

HNO₃ is a strong acid, so it dissociates completely and [H⁺] = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. pH is defined as −log₁₀[H⁺] = −log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3. The values 11 and 13 would describe strongly basic solutions (pH 14 − 3), which is the mirror-image trap.

HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄ and HBr are all strong acids that dissociate essentially completely in water. Acetic acid, CH₃COOH, is the only weak acid in the list: it establishes an equilibrium in which most molecules remain undissociated.

Bond polarity grows with the electronegativity difference between the two atoms. Using Pauling values, O (3.44) versus H (2.20) differs by about 1.2, N (3.04) versus H by about 0.8, C (2.55) versus H by about 0.4, while C-C and H-H join identical atoms and are completely non-polar. The O-H bond therefore shows the largest charge separation.

Boyle's law states pV = constant for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, which means pressure is inversely proportional to volume: doubling the volume halves the pressure. Direct proportionality to volume contradicts the law, and proportionality to temperature or moles describes different, non-isothermal or non-fixed-amount conditions.

The mass number 23 counts protons plus neutrons and changes between isotopes, but the proton number is fixed by the element's atomic number. Sodium's atomic number is 11, so every sodium atom has 11 protons (and in this isotope 23 − 11 = 12 neutrons). The answers 23 or 12 confuse the mass number or neutron count with the proton count.

Alkenes contain one C=C double bond and follow the general formula CnH2n. C₂H₄ (ethene) fits this formula exactly and is the alkene. CH₄, C₂H₆ and C₃H₈ are saturated alkanes fitting CnH2n+2, and C₆H₆ is the aromatic benzene ring, which is not classified as an alkene.
Alcohols are defined by a hydroxyl group, -OH, bonded to a saturated carbon, as in ethanol CH₃CH₂OH. The -CHO group marks aldehydes, -COOH carboxylic acids, -CO- ketones, and -NH₂ amines.

A carbonyl group (C=O) whose carbon is bonded to two other carbons inside the chain is the defining feature of a ketone, as in propanone CH₃-CO-CH₃. In an aldehyde the carbonyl carbon is terminal and carries a hydrogen, and in a carboxylic acid it is additionally bonded to an -OH.

A higher reactant concentration means more particles per unit volume, so collisions occur more frequently and more particles per second possess the energy and orientation needed to react, raising the rate. Concentration does not change the activation energy, which is a fixed property of the reaction pathway, and it does not shift the equilibrium constant K, which only temperature can change.

ΔH measures the enthalpy change of the system; endothermic means the system absorbs heat, so the products end up higher in enthalpy than the reactants and ΔH is positive. The sign convention is the reverse for exothermic reactions. ΔH also cannot equal ΔS (a quantity in J/K) or the activation energy, which measures the barrier height rather than the overall energy change.

Carbon-14 contains two more neutrons than the stable isotopes ¹²C and ¹³C and decays by beta emission with a half-life of about 5730 years, which is the basis of radiocarbon dating. ¹⁶O and ¹⁴N are stable nuclides, so carbon-14 is the only radioactive species listed.

At 25 °C neutrality corresponds to pH 7, where [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷ M. A pH of 8 means [H⁺] = 10⁻⁸ M, ten times fewer hydrogen ions than neutral water, so the solution is mildly (weakly) basic. Strongly basic solutions lie well above pH 10, and anything below 7 would be acidic.

When multiplying powers with the same base, exponents add: 2³ × 2² = 2³⁺² = 2⁵ = 32. Arithmetic check: 8 × 4 = 32, confirming the result. The value 2⁶ adds one exponent too many, 4⁵ wrongly changes the base instead of adding exponents, and 8 is just 2³ alone.
log₁₀(x) = 2 asks for the number whose base-10 logarithm is 2, i.e. 10 raised to the power 2. Converting from log to exponential form gives x = 10² = 100. Check: log₁₀(100) = log₁₀(10 × 10) = 2.

x² = 49 has two real solutions, x = 7 and x = −7, since both square to 49. The condition x > 0 discards the negative root, leaving x = √49 = 7. The value 14 mistakes doubling for square-rooting, and 24.5 divides 49 by 2 instead of taking the root.

Step 1: add 1 to both sides, giving x/3 ≥ 3. Step 2: multiply both sides by 3; since 3 is positive the inequality direction is unchanged, so x ≥ 9. Boundary check: at x = 9 the left side is 9/3 − 1 = 2, which satisfies the ≥ condition, and any larger x works while any smaller x fails.

A square has four equal sides, so the side length is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. The area is side squared: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². The value 100 cm² comes from wrongly squaring the perimeter, and 20 cm² confuses the perimeter with the area.

In a right triangle with angles 30°, 60°, 90° the sides opposite them are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, and for 60° the adjacent side is the shortest leg, so cos 60° = 1/2. The value √3/2 belongs to cos 30°, the classic mix-up.

Two coin tosses give four equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one outcome (two tails) contains no head, so P(no head) = 1/4 and P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. Alternatively, HT, TH and HH are the three favourable outcomes out of four. The value 1/2 treats the event as if only one toss mattered.
Step 1: use a = Δv ÷ t = (v_final − v_initial) ÷ t. Step 2: substitute the data: (0 − 20) ÷ 5 = −4 m/s². The negative sign indicates slowing down, so the deceleration has magnitude 4 m/s².

For resistors in parallel the reciprocals add: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. Equivalent shortcut: n equal resistors R in parallel give R/n, here 6/3 = 2 Ω. The value 18 Ω is the series combination, the classic trap for this arrangement.

Ohm's law gives V = I × R. Substituting: V = 0.5 A × 10 Ω = 5 V. The value 0.05 V results from dividing the current by the resistance instead of multiplying, and 50 V moves the decimal point the wrong way.
Kinetic energy is KE = ½mv² = ½ × 0.5 kg × (4 m/s)² = 0.25 × 16 = 4 J. The value 2 J comes from computing mv without squaring the speed, and 16 J would be mv² without the factor of ½.

Work equals force times the distance moved in the direction of the force: W = F × d = 10 N × 5 m = 50 J. The value 2 J comes from dividing instead of multiplying, and 0 J would only be correct if the force acted perpendicular to the motion.

Use the heating relation Q = m × c × ΔT with m = 2 kg, c = 4200 J/(kg·°C) and ΔT = 10 °C: Q = 2 × 4200 × 10 = 84,000 J (84 kJ). The value 42,000 J drops the factor of 2 from the mass, and 840 J is a decimal-place error.
